title: Bug: robust CPU-loading tests with "yes" on weak-per-core platforms
author: yanmarkman
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

PTF tests using CPU stress (yes) leak CPU hogs when DUT is slow, because cleanup does not run in pytest teardown.

On Weak-per-core platforms (for Example -- Nokia-7215/armhf) PTF tests with construction
    for i in range(host_vcpus):   duthost.shell("nohup yes > /dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 1")
are ABORTED by timeout before achieving   duthost.shell("killall yes"),
leaving "yes" processes forever.

Make these tests robust to keep the board/platform alive with possibility to continue test-sequence
Requires these tests should start a watchdog protector before starting
     duthost.shell("nohup yes > /dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 1"):
------------------------------------------------------------------
WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT = ?????   # seconds depending upon the test
# Start watchdog that guarantees cleanup even if test aborts
duthost.shell(
    "nohup sh -c 'sleep {0}; pkill -9 yes' >/dev/null 2>&1 &".format(WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT)
)
# Start CPU hog
for i in range(host_vcpus):
    duthost.shell("nohup yes > /dev/null 2>&1 &")
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Tests to be expanded 
tests/pc/test_po_cleanup.py
tests/pc/test_po_update.py
tests/qos/test_cpu_storm.py
tests/qos/test_buffer_storm.py
tests/cacl/test_control_plane_acl.py
tests/pc/test_lacp_stress.py
tests/common/helpers/cpu_stress.py
tests/common/helpers/storm.py







### Steps to Reproduce

On Nokia-7215(armhf)-board with TRIXE-image
run 202511 PTF test test_po_cleanup.py.
The test failed upon timeout, aborted and exited before calling for the 

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual: test fail-and-exited but all Cores/CPU s are 100% busy
Expected: test fail but board returns to normal CPU loading

linkedPullRequests.title: [snmp][pc] Add watchdog for CPU stress cleanup on test abort
linkedPullRequests.author: rustiqly
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
[agent]
Add a background watchdog process that kills `yes` CPU hogs after a timeout, even if the test is aborted before reaching the `finally` block.

On weak-per-core platforms (e.g. Nokia-7215/armhf), PTF tests using `yes` for CPU stress can be killed by pytest timeout before cleanup runs, leaving `yes` processes running forever and making the platform unusable for subsequent tests.

**Affected tests:**
- `tests/snmp/test_snmp_cpu.py` — watchdog timeout: 300s (5 min)
- `tests/pc/test_po_cleanup.py` — watchdog timeout: 600s (10 min, accounts for config_reload wait)

The watchdog uses `nohup sh -c 'sleep N; pkill -9 yes'` to guarantee cleanup regardless of test outcome. The existing `finally` block still handles normal cleanup; the watchdog is a safety net for abnormal termination.

Fixes: #21517

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix

### How did you test it?
```
AST parse verification: OK (both files)
Verified watchdog command spawns before CPU hog processes
Verified existing finally blocks are preserved unchanged
```
